DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 46 s. 2022 June 3, 2022 ATTY. SYLVAN GERALD L. SABIO Unit F., 2nd Floor, Uptown corner Building B-2, L-2, Golden Glow North Commercial Macapagal Road, Upper Carmen Cagayan de Oro City Dear Atty. Sabio: This has reference to your letter requesting for legal opinion relative to the enforceability of the Decision of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan in Administrative Case No. 01-21 for Abuse of Authority and Grave Misconduct, etc. entitled "Lorenzo C. Takang, Kabaluna G. Salik, Jr., Kim Peter L. Pluma vs. Mayor Alicia R. Ty, Vice-Mayor Rolando Manuel C. Ty, Et Al. " Per your letter, on 07 January 2022, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Misamis Occidental rendered a Decision (SP Decision, for brevity) in the above-entitled case imposing a penalty of suspension for a period of six (6) months upon the respondents. The aforesaid SP Decision was received by the respondents on 08 January 2022. On 01 January 2022, respondents filed a Motion for Reconsideration and the same was filed via electronic mailing. Since the SP has not yet resolve the respondents' Motion for Reconsideration, they were constrained to file a Notice of Appeal on 18 January 2018 via electronic mailing. The foregoing is compounded by the fact that the SP Decision, which carries the penalty of suspension, shall be enforced on 10 January 2022 or within the election period pursuant to COMELEC Resolution No. 10742. Hence, your query. In this regard, may we invite your attention to Sections 61 , 66, 67 and 68 of RA 7160 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC), which provide: "SECTION 61. Form and Filing of Administrative Complaints. — A verified complaint against any erring local elective official shall be prepared as follows: Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

(b) A complaint against any elective official of a municipality shall be filed before the Sangguniang Panlalawigan whose decision may be appealed to the Office of the President; xxx "SECTION 66. Form and Notice of Decision. - (a) The investigation of the case shall be terminated within ninety (90) days from the start thereof. Within thirty (30) days after the end of the investigation, the Office of the President or the Sanggunian concemed shall render a decision in writing stating clearly and distinctly the facts and the reasons for such decision. Copies of said decision shall immediately be fumished the respondent and all interested parties (b) The penalty of suspension shall not exceed the unexpired term of the respondent or a period of six (6) months for every administrative offense, nor shall said penalty be a bar to the candidacy of the respondent so suspended as long as he meets the qualifications required for the office. (c) The penalty of removal from office as a result of an administrative investigation shall be considered a bar to the candidacy of the respondent for any elective position." Decisions in "SECTION 67. Administrative Appeals administrative cases may, within thirty (30) days from receipt thereof, be appealed to the following: (a) The Sangguniang Panlalawigan. in the case of decisions of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of component cities and the Sangguniang bayan; and (b) The Office of the President, in the case of decisions of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan and the Sangguniang Panlungsod of highly urbanized cities and independent component cities. Decisions of the Office of the President shall be final and executory." "SECTION 68. Execution Pending Appeal. - An appeal shall not prevent a decision from becoming final or executory. The respondent shall be considered as having been placed under preventive suspension during the pendency of an appeal in the event he wins such appeal. In the event the appeal results in an exoneration, he shall be paid his salary and such other emoluments during the pendency of the appeal." Based on the foregoing, a verified complaint against any erring any elective official of a municipality shall be filed before the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. After the Sangguniang Panlalawigan decided the administrative case within the time specified in the aforequoted provisions, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan may direct the Governor to implement its decision. If the Govemor is being directed by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan to implement its decision or judgment rendered pursuant to the exercise of its quasi-judicial powers conferred by Section 61 of the LGC, it is the ministerial duty of the Governor to execute the same and he/she has no discretion to determine the propriety of the implementation of the decision or judgment. Page 2 of 4

The service or implementation of the decision/judgment has to be made without unnecessary delay so that after being duly informed, the respondent can immediately take steps to protect his interest by filing an appeal or apply for other appropriate relief. In this regard, please be informed that in a Memorandum from the Executive Secretary dated December 01, 2021 re APPELLATE JURISDICTION OF THE OFFICE OF THE PRESIDENT OVER SUSPENSION ORDERS AGAINST LOCAL ELECTIVE OFFICIALS, the Department was advised, among others, that the Office of the President "xxx has authority to order the stay of execution of the final decisions or orders of suspension from office issued by the Sanggunians against local elective officials, pursuant to Section 9 of AO No. 22 and consistent with the Supreme Court ruling in Berces Sr. v. Executive Secretary. " As you represented, a copy of the 07 January 2022 Decision of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan was received by the Respondents on 08 January 2022 (Saturday). Section 15 of the COMELEC Resolution No. 10742 re IN THE MATTER OF THE ENFRCEMENT OF THE PROHIBITION AGAINST APPOINTMENT OR HIRING OF NEW EMPLOYEES; CREATION OR FILLING UP OF NEW POSITIONS; GIVING SALARY INCREASES; TRANSFER OR DETAIL OF CIVIL SERVICE EMPLOYEES; SUSPENSIONOF ELECTIVE LOCAL OFFICIALS; AND FILING OF LEAVE OF ABSENCES OF LOCAL TREASURERS IN CONNECTION WITH THE MA Y 09, 2022 NA TIONAL AND LOCAL ELECTIONS, reads: "SECTION 15. Prohibited Acts.—From January 09. 2022, Sunday to June 08. 2022. Wednesday. the provisions of law to the contrary notwithstanding, no public official shall, except upon prior written approval of the Commission. suspend any elective provincial. city, municipal or baranqav officer. Consistent with Section 2 (h) hereof, the ban shall include preventive suspension or suspension imposed as a penalty. No prior approval is required if the suspension will be for purposes of applying the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act in relation to the suspension and removal of elective officials." (Emphasis Supplied) As represented to the Central Office by Representative Diego "Nonoy" Ty, First District of Misamis Occidental, notwithstanding the failure of the Govemor to issue an order implementing the 07 January 2022 Decision of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Misamis Occidental, respondents undertook to heed to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan Decision by voluntarily vacating their posts and turned them over to the next-in-rank Sangguniang Bayan Members. As stated, the respondents received their copies of the SP Decision on 08 January 2022 or a day before the start of the election period in connection with the 09 May 2022 National and Local Elections. From receipt thereof and without waiting the implementation order from the Governor, respondents voluntarily commenced the service of their suspension order. Page 3 of 4

The executory nature of the decisions rendered by the sanggunians, notwithstanding an appeal, was made explicit in the first sentence of Section 68 of the Local Government Code of 1991. We are of the view that despite the absence of an order from the Governor implementing the Sangguniang Panlalawigan Decision, the respondents can voluntarily vacate their respective posts and serve their suspension order. Incidents of voluntary service of suspension are no longer new to the Department. There were several •local elective officials who had previously undertook to voluntarily serve their suspension involving cases filed before the Sandiganbayan. The Department sees no reason why said voluntary service could not be applied in administrative cases. In the instant case, the reason for the failure of the Governor to issue an order implementing the January 7, 2022 Decision of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Misamis Occidental against the respondents was not stated. However, if the reason given by the Governor is for him to seek clearance first from the COMELEC in view of the onset of election period on January 9, 2022, then the Governor is justified for not immediately implementing the SP Decision. Once given clearance by the COMELEC or the lapse of the election period, whichever comes earlier, he can already cause the implementation of the SP Decision. However, we would like to emphasize that if the respondents so desire to voluntarily serve their suspension orders on the day of their receipt of the SP Decision and without waiting the implementation order from the Governor, we reiterate that they can do so pursuant to the executory nature of the SP Decision. It is respectfully reminded however that the respondents' willingness to voluntarily serve their suspension to compiy with the orders of Sangguniang Panlalawigan must be rrianifested first in writing to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for record purposes. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, By the Authority of the Secretary: AN Undersec ry for Local Governm t OUSLG/MLl/LLLS-LRALLD/Glp M. AGABE Copy furnished: Regional Director, DILG-Region X Km3 Fr. W.F.
